chapters.1.lds: The selected lesson teaches that apostles receive their call through revelation. Why does the replacement need to have accompanied Jesus’ whole ministry?
chapters.1.summary: The writer opens a second book for Theophilus. The risen Jesus teaches the apostles for forty days. He tells them to wait in Jerusalem for the Holy Spirit. They ask if he will now restore the kingdom to Israel. He is taken up, and two men in white speak to them. About 120 believers pray together in an upper room. Peter says another witness must take the place of Judas. They pray and cast lots, and the lot falls on Matthias.
chapters.2.lds: The selected lesson connects the Spirit’s prompting with action. How does baptism lead into shared meals and care for needs?
chapters.2.summary: On the day of Pentecost a sound like wind fills the house. Tongues like fire rest on the believers, and they speak in other languages. Jews from many nations hear their own languages. Some are amazed, and others say the speakers are drunk. Peter quotes Joel and says God raised Jesus from the dead. The hearers ask what they should do. Peter tells them to repent and be baptized. About three thousand join, and they share teaching, meals, prayer, and goods.
chapters.3.lds: The selected lesson studies bold witness through the Holy Ghost. Why does Peter refuse credit for the man’s changed condition?
chapters.3.summary: Peter and John go to the temple at the hour of prayer. A man lame from birth asks them for money at the gate. Peter says he has no silver or gold. He tells the man to walk in the name of Jesus Christ. The man leaps, walks, and praises God in the temple. A crowd runs together in Solomon’s porch. Peter says God raised Jesus, whom they had denied. He says they acted in ignorance and calls them to repent.
chapters.4.lds: The selected lesson teaches the Spirit’s help in courageous witness. How does the healed man’s presence affect the council’s options?
chapters.4.summary: The priests, the temple captain, and the Sadducees arrest Peter and John. The next day the rulers ask by what name they acted. Peter says the man stands healed by the name of Jesus. The council sees their boldness and notes they are untrained men. It orders them not to speak in Jesus’ name. Peter and John say they cannot stop telling what they saw. The believers pray for boldness, and the place shakes. They share goods, and Barnabas sells a field for those in need.
chapters.5.lds: The selected lesson studies continued witness despite opposition. Why does Peter distinguish ownership from the lie about the sale?
chapters.5.summary: Ananias and Sapphira sell land and keep part of the price. They bring the rest as if it were the whole. Peter says Ananias lied to God, and Ananias falls dead. Three hours later Sapphira repeats the lie and also dies. The apostles heal many in Solomon’s porch. The high priest and the Sadducees jail them, but an angel opens the doors. Before the council Peter says they must obey God rather than men. Gamaliel advises caution, and the apostles are beaten and released.
chapters.6.lds: How does the whole group help answer the widows’ complaint?
chapters.6.summary: The number of disciples grows. The Hellenists, Jewish believers who spoke Greek, complain against the Hebrews. Their widows are being missed in the daily serving. The twelve ask the group to choose seven men for this work. The group chooses Stephen, Philip, and five others, and the apostles lay hands on them. The word spreads, and many priests believe. Stephen works signs, and men from a synagogue argue with him. They bring false witnesses and take him before the council.
chapters.7.lds: The selected lesson warns against resisting the Holy Ghost. How does Stephen’s final prayer answer the violence against him?
chapters.7.summary: The high priest asks Stephen if the charges are true. Stephen answers with Israel’s history. God appeared to Abraham in Mesopotamia and was with Joseph in Egypt. Moses was pushed away by his own people, yet God sent him. The fathers made a calf in the wilderness. They had the tabernacle, and Solomon built a house. Stephen says his hearers resist the Holy Spirit as their fathers did. They stone him, and he prays that the sin not be held against them.
chapters.8.lds: The selected lesson connects the Spirit’s guidance with helping others understand Jesus. How does the official’s question differ from Simon’s request for power?
chapters.8.summary: Saul approves of Stephen’s death, and a great persecution scatters the believers. Philip tells the people of Samaria about Christ, and many are baptized. Simon, who had amazed the city with sorcery, is baptized too. Peter and John come and lay hands on them, and they receive the Holy Spirit. Simon offers money for that power, and Peter rebukes him. An angel sends Philip to a desert road. An Ethiopian official is reading Isaiah in his chariot. Philip tells him about Jesus and baptizes him.
chapters.9.lds: The selected lesson teaches that people can repent and change. Why does Ananias name his fear before approaching Saul?
chapters.9.summary: Saul travels to Damascus with letters to arrest followers of the Way. A light from the sky stops him, and a voice says it is Jesus. He is blind for three days. The Lord sends a disciple named Ananias to him. Ananias lays hands on Saul, and Saul sees and is baptized. Saul speaks of Jesus in the synagogues, and opponents plot to kill him. Barnabas brings him to the apostles in Jerusalem. Peter heals Aeneas in Lydda and raises Tabitha in Joppa.
chapters.10.lds: The selected lesson teaches God’s acceptance across peoples and gradual revelation. What does the Spirit’s arrival change before Peter orders baptism?
chapters.10.summary: Cornelius is a centurion in Caesarea who fears God and gives to the poor. An angel tells him to send for Peter in Joppa. Peter sees a sheet full of animals and hears a voice tell him to eat. He refuses, and the voice says not to call unclean what God cleansed. The Spirit tells him to go with the messengers. In Cornelius’s house Peter says God shows no favoritism. The Holy Spirit falls on the Gentile hearers while he speaks. Peter orders that they be baptized.
chapters.11.lds: The selected lesson studies Peter’s explanation as part of gradual revelation. Why does Peter compare the household’s gift with the group’s own beginning?
chapters.11.summary: Believers in Jerusalem criticize Peter for eating with uncircumcised men. Peter tells them the vision, the Spirit’s order, and the angel’s message to Cornelius. He says the Spirit fell on that household as on them at the beginning. They fall silent and then glorify God. Scattered believers reach Antioch, and some speak to Greeks. Barnabas comes, and he brings Saul from Tarsus. The disciples are first called Christians in Antioch. They send famine relief to Judea by Barnabas and Saul.
chapters.12.lds: Why does the praying group struggle to believe Rhoda’s report?
chapters.12.summary: King Herod kills James the brother of John with the sword. He arrests Peter during the days of unleavened bread. The assembly prays for Peter. At night an angel wakes him, the chains fall off, and the iron gate opens. Peter goes to the house of Mary, mother of John Mark. A servant named Rhoda hears his voice and runs in without opening the gate. Herod orders the guards put to death. Later he accepts praise as a god, and an angel strikes him.
chapters.13.lds: How does the next Sabbath’s crowd change the earlier invitation’s outcome?
chapters.13.summary: The Holy Spirit tells the assembly at Antioch to set apart Barnabas and Saul. On Cyprus the sorcerer Elymas opposes them and is struck blind. The proconsul Sergius Paulus believes. In Antioch of Pisidia the synagogue rulers invite Paul to speak. He tells Israel’s history from Egypt to David and says God raised Jesus. The next Sabbath almost the whole city gathers. Some Jewish hearers contradict Paul, and he turns to the Gentiles. The two are driven out and go on to Iconium.
chapters.14.lds: How do the teachers answer praise that gives them divine status?
chapters.14.summary: In Iconium Paul and Barnabas speak in the synagogue, and the city divides. They flee a plan to stone them. In Lystra Paul heals a man who had never walked. The crowd calls them Jupiter and Mercury, and a priest brings oxen to sacrifice. The two tear their clothes and say they are only men. Opponents from Antioch and Iconium arrive, and the crowd stones Paul. He gets up and goes on to Derbe. They return through the cities, appoint elders, and report in Antioch.
chapters.15.lds: The selected lesson studies the meeting’s decision through continuing revelation. Why do trusted messengers accompany the written decision?
chapters.15.summary: Men from Judea teach in Antioch that Gentiles must be circumcised to be saved. Paul and Barnabas dispute this and go to Jerusalem. The apostles and elders meet. Peter says God gave the Gentiles the Spirit and made no distinction. James quotes the prophets and proposes four things to avoid. They send a letter with Judas and Silas, and Antioch rejoices. Paul and Barnabas then disagree over John Mark and part ways. Paul takes Silas through Syria and Cilicia.
chapters.16.lds: The selected lesson teaches spiritual guidance and courage when sharing the gospel. How does rescue from suicide lead toward teaching, washed wounds, and a meal?
chapters.16.summary: Paul takes Timothy with him from Lystra. A vision of a man from Macedonia calls Paul across the sea. In Philippi Lydia, a seller of purple, believes and hosts them. Paul orders a spirit out of a slave girl who told fortunes. Her owners lose their income and accuse Paul and Silas before the magistrates. The two are beaten and jailed, and an earthquake opens the doors at midnight. The jailer and his household are baptized. Paul says they are Romans, and the magistrates come and ask them to leave.
chapters.17.lds: The selected lesson teaches that people are God’s children. Why does Paul begin the Athens speech with the hearers’ worship and poetry?
chapters.17.summary: In Thessalonica Paul reasons from the Scriptures for three Sabbaths. Some believe, and opponents raise a mob against Jason’s house. In Beroea the hearers examine the Scriptures daily. In Athens Paul is troubled by the city’s idols. Epicurean and Stoic philosophers bring him to the Areopagus. He speaks of the God who made the world and needs nothing. He quotes their poets and says God will judge through a man he raised. Some mock, some want to hear more, and a few believe.
chapters.18.lds: The selected lesson studies courage during Paul’s extended teaching. How does private correction prepare Apollos to help other believers?
chapters.18.summary: In Corinth Paul lives and works with Aquila and Priscilla, who are tentmakers. He reasons in the synagogue each Sabbath. When opposed, he moves next door to the house of Titius Justus. Crispus, the synagogue ruler, believes. The Lord tells Paul in a vision not to be afraid. The proconsul Gallio refuses to judge a dispute about Jewish law. Paul sails to Ephesus, Caesarea, and Antioch. In Ephesus Apollos teaches well but knows only John’s baptism.
chapters.19.lds: How does Demetrius connect income with religious honor in his appeal?
chapters.19.summary: In Ephesus Paul meets twelve disciples who know only John’s baptism. He baptizes them in Jesus’ name, and they receive the Holy Spirit. He teaches for two years in the school of Tyrannus. Seven sons of Sceva misuse Jesus’ name, and a possessed man beats them. Many burn their books of magic. Demetrius, a silversmith who makes shrines of Artemis, gathers the craftsmen. A crowd fills the theater and shouts for two hours. The town clerk sends them home and points to the courts.
chapters.20.lds: Why does Paul connect his own labor with helping weak people?
chapters.20.summary: Paul travels through Macedonia and Greece and returns by way of Troas. There Paul speaks until midnight, and young Eutychus falls from a window. Paul embraces him, and he is brought in alive. At Miletus Paul calls the elders of Ephesus. He says he taught them openly and house to house. He expects chains in Jerusalem and says they will not see him again. He warns of wolves and tells them to guard the flock. They kneel, pray, and weep.
chapters.21.lds: Which accusation comes from an assumption rather than witnessed temple entry?
chapters.21.summary: Paul sails to Tyre and then to Caesarea, where he stays with Philip. The prophet Agabus binds his own hands and feet with Paul’s belt. He says Paul will be bound in Jerusalem. Paul says he is ready to die there. James and the elders report a rumor that he teaches Jews to leave Moses. They ask him to join four men in a vow at the temple. Men from Asia see him there and stir up the crowd. Roman soldiers take him, and he asks to speak.
chapters.22.lds: The selected lesson studies testimony through Paul’s recalled encounter. Which recalled instruction makes the listening crowd demand Paul’s removal?
chapters.22.summary: Paul speaks to the crowd in Hebrew, and they grow quiet. He says he is a Jew, taught by Gamaliel, and once persecuted the Way. He tells of the light near Damascus and the voice of Jesus. Ananias, a devout man, told him he would be a witness. Later, praying in the temple, he was told to leave Jerusalem. When he says he was sent to the Gentiles, the crowd shouts for his death. The officer orders him flogged. Paul says he is a Roman citizen by birth, and they stop.
chapters.23.lds: How does the nephew’s report change the planned journey?
chapters.23.summary: Paul tells the council he has lived in good conscience. The high priest Ananias orders him struck. Paul says he is a Pharisee, on trial for the hope of resurrection. Pharisees and Sadducees then argue, and the officer pulls him out. That night the Lord tells him he must testify in Rome. More than forty men vow not to eat until they kill him. Paul’s nephew reports the plot to the officer. Soldiers take Paul by night to the governor Felix in Caesarea.
chapters.24.lds: How do fear and hoped-for money affect Felix’s delay?
chapters.24.summary: The high priest Ananias and a speaker named Tertullus bring charges before Felix. Tertullus calls Paul a plague and a leader of the Nazarene sect. He says Paul tried to profane the temple. Paul answers that no one found him arguing or stirring a crowd. He says he worships the God of his fathers and hopes for a resurrection. Felix puts off the case until Lysias comes. He and his wife Drusilla hear Paul, and Felix becomes afraid. He keeps Paul two years and leaves him bound.
chapters.25.lds: Why does Festus still need a clear charge after Paul’s appeal?
chapters.25.summary: Festus replaces Felix, and the chief priests ask him to send Paul to Jerusalem. They plan an ambush on the road. Festus hears the case in Caesarea, and the charges are not proved. He asks if Paul will be tried in Jerusalem. Paul says he stands at Caesar’s court and appeals to Caesar. Festus agrees to send him. King Agrippa and Bernice visit, and Festus explains the case. He brings Paul before them the next day.
chapters.26.lds: The selected lesson connects testimony with service to others. Why does Paul exclude his chains from what he wishes for his hearers?
chapters.26.summary: Paul speaks before King Agrippa, Bernice, and Festus. He says he lived as a Pharisee and now stands trial for Israel’s hope. He tells how he jailed the saints and voted for their deaths. He describes the light on the Damascus road and the voice of Jesus. He says he obeyed the vision and taught Jews and Gentiles to repent. Festus shouts that learning has made him mad. Paul asks Agrippa if he believes the prophets. Agrippa says Paul could have been freed if he had not appealed.
chapters.27.lds: The selected lesson applies the voyage to following the Lord’s servants. Why do promised lives still require the sailors to remain aboard?
chapters.27.summary: Paul sails for Italy under a centurion named Julius. At Fair Havens he warns that the voyage will bring loss. The centurion follows the pilot and the owner, and they sail on. A violent wind drives the ship for many days. Paul says an angel told him no life will be lost. On the fourteenth night the sailors try to leave in the boat. Paul urges all 276 people to eat. The ship breaks up on a shore, and everyone reaches land.
chapters.28.lds: Why does the book end with teaching rather than the appeal’s final verdict?
chapters.28.summary: The survivors land on Malta, and the islanders show them kindness. A viper bites Paul, and he shakes it off unharmed. He heals the father of Publius and others. After three months they sail to Italy, and believers meet Paul on the road. In Rome Paul lives under guard and calls the Jewish leaders. He explains his case and teaches them from morning to evening. Some believe, and some do not. Paul quotes Isaiah, and for two years he receives all who come.
